newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT-Motorola reports lower Q4 profit.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT-Motorola reports lower Q4 profit.

text.p: Motorola Inc, which reported fourth quarter earnings Thursday, issued the following comments as part of its earnings report. The company reported fourth quarter net income of $238 million, or $0.39 per share on a diluted basis, compared to $432 million or $0.72 per share the year earlier. A full version of the company's earnings table ran separately.
Business Editors, Computers and Telecommunications Writers
SCHAUMBURG, Ill.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Jan. 9, 1997--Motorola, Inc. today reported higher sales and lower earnings for the full year 1996.

Sales rose 3 percent to $28.0 billion from $27.0 billion in 1995. Earnings were $1.15 billion, compared with $1.78 billion a year earlier. Fully diluted earnings per common and common equivalent share were $1.90, compared with $2.93 in 1995. Net margin on sales was 4.1 percent for the full year 1996, compared with 6.6 percent a year ago.

Fourth quarter sales were $7.7 billion, up 5 percent from $7.3 billion in the fourth quarter of 1995. Net earnings were $238 million, compared with $432 million a year ago. Fully diluted earnings per common and common equivalent share were 39 cents, compared with 72 cents a year ago. The 1996 fourth quarter results include tens of millions of dollars of restructuring costs, as was indicated after the third quarter, as well as other unusual charges for the period, resulting in a combined negative impact to pre-tax earnings of more than $150 million. Net margin on sales was 3.1 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996 compared with 5.9 percent for the year-earlier period.

Robert L. Growney, president and chief operating officer, indicated that the unusual charges relate to various asset writedowns and strategic decisions to end certain technology development programs that no longer offer sufficient growth potential to justify further investment.
Growney reviewed the following results of Motorola's major operations compared with 1995: General Systems Segment
For the year, segment sales advanced 6 percent to $11.3 billion, orders rose 15 percent and segment operating profits were lower.

For the fourth quarter, sales rose 17 percent to $3.3 billion, orders were up 21 percent and operating profits were higher. Cellular Subscriber Sector (CSS) orders increased, led by significant growth in Europe and the Americas. Cellular Infrastructure Group (CIG) orders were also higher, with significant growth in the Americas and Asia-Pacific regions. Orders in Japan, for both CSS and CIG, were lower. Computer Group orders were up significantly.

Motorola announced its Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM) StarTAC(TM) wearable digital cellular telephone, the world's lightest and smallest phone for GSM networks. It is shipping to several key GSM markets throughout the world.

Other product announcements included the first GSM cellular telephone to provide Chinese character short messaging, and the latest version of the Easy Mobile Office data product, which includes the MicroTAC(R) International 8700 GSM phone and a PC card offering throughput of up to 36,000 bits per second.
Total unit volume shipments of Motorola in the GSM phone category were up significantly in the fourth quarter and have risen steadily throughout each quarter in 1996.

CIG increased its Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) leadership by deploying commercial CDMA networks for operators in San Diego, Chicago, Milwaukee, Austin, San Antonio, Dallas, Fort Worth, Honolulu and Lima, Peru. Motorola became the first company to incorporate short-message service in its CDMA digital networks.
The group won contracts for GSM networks in China, India, Kuwait and Turkey; for fixed wireless systems in the Philippines, Nigeria and Yemen; and for analog cellular networks in Brazil.

The Motorola Computer Group enhanced its StarMax(TM) family of computers with a model based on the PowerPC 603e(TM) microprocessor running at 240 megahertz. Significant shipments of computers compatible with the Mac(R) OS operating system began in the fourth quarter. Semiconductor Products Segment
For the year, segment sales declined 8 percent to $7.9 billion, orders were down 22 percent and segment operating profits were lower.

For the fourth quarter, sales were down 18 percent to $1.9 billion, orders declined 11 percent, and the segment had an operating loss versus a profit a year ago. Excluding unusual charges, the segment's profitability would have improved versus the third quarter and the segment would have reported a small operating profit.

Orders were lower in all regions compared with the fourth quarter of 1995. Among major market segments, orders improved in personal computer/workstation and in communications. Distributor orders were lower. Compared with the third quarter of 1996, orders improved in all regions, as well as most market segments and distribution.

In automotive electronics, when General Motors delivered its first EV1 electric vehicle to California and Arizona in December, each auto included more than 700 Motorola semiconductors in power-train, on-board charger and auxiliary power module applications. Motorola also introduced 32- and 64-bit microcontrollers that support the controller area network standard for auto diagnostics and power-train control.

Motorola announced a smartcard microchip that does not require physical contact between the card and the card reader and the award of European Union funding for a joint research and development program with Gemplus for a new generation of microprocessor-based contactless cards that are compatible with existing contact readers and terminals. A prime use will be contactless ticketing for bus and rail commuters. Also introduced was a carbon monoxide sensing device for residential, commercial, industrial and environmental applications.

Under an agreement with Mitsubishi Electric Corp., Motorola will exchange certain microprocessor technologies for Mitsubishi's embedded dynamic random access memory (DRAM) design and process technologies. In another agreement, Motorola and Mitsubishi will jointly market flash memory devices for portable and hand-held applications. Messaging, Information and Media Segment
Segment sales for the full year rose 8 percent to $4.0 billion, orders declined 3 percent and operating profits were lower for the year.

Fourth quarter sales declined 17 percent to $876 million, orders were 24 percent lower, and the segment had an operating loss compared with a profit a year ago, due to the decline in sales, pricing pressures in the modem business and restructuring/unusual charges.

Management believes that the reason for lower fourth quarter orders for paging products in North America was that paging operators reduced inventories in order to improve their financial positions and cash flow. Management also believes that sales by operators to consumers in North America during the quarter continued to grow. Paging orders in China were significantly higher compared with a year ago, as well as with the third quarter of 1996, when an inventory correction was occurring in that market.

Motorola's high-speed Flex(TM) messaging protocol has been adopted by operators in more than 30 countries. New Flex messaging systems were implemented in the Philippines, Indonesia, Thailand and Colombia.

AMTEL de PR announced a voice messaging system in Puerto Rico that will use Motorola's Tenor(TM) voice personal communicator, which enables users to store and play back voice messages. The system will employ the InFLEXion(TM) messaging protocol. PageNet demonstrated its VoiceNow(R) system in the Dallas-Fort Worth area.

The Information Systems Group introduced the first in a series of software-based communications products, a V.34 data/fax/voice host-based modem that uses a computer's central processing unit to perform modem functions.
The Multimedia Group, with the addition of U S West and Cox Communications, now has cable modem agreements in place with the top six U.S. multiple-system operators.
The Wireless Data Group announced support of the Personal Messenger family of wireless modem cards for handheld computers based on the Microsoft Windows(R) CE platform. Land Mobile Products Segment
Segment sales for the year rose 11 percent to $4.0 billion, orders increased 16 percent, and operating profits were higher.

Fourth-quarter sales increased 26 percent to $1.3 billion, orders were 26 percent higher, and operating profits improved. Orders were higher for both analog equipment and digital systems and products. Orders for Integrated Dispatch Enhanced Network (iDEN(TM)) equipment were up significantly, including $132 million from Nextel Communications, Inc. as part of the continued rollout of its nationwide system in the U.S. Other iDEN equipment orders came from Southern Communications in the U.S., Clearnet Communications in Canada, Movicom in Argentina and Infocom in the Philippines. iDEN communication service was expanded in Japan and launched in Singapore.

Major orders for ASTRO(R) digital two-way radio equipment were received in Switzerland and from the City of Calgary in Canada, the State of Florida and the U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Service. Other major U.S. orders were received in Kansas and Maryland.
Major systems awards were also received for a citywide system in Rome, Italy, and from utility and public safety customers in Mexico, the Bahamas, Guatemala and Panama.

New products included a mobile two-way radio for Eastern European countries and a new portable radio for on-site communications in Germany, Sweden and The Netherlands. Automotive, Energy and Components Sector

For the year, sector sales declined 5 percent, orders were 5 percent lower, and operating profits were lower. Results for the sector, formerly the Automotive, Energy and Controls Group, are part of the "Other Products" segment.

In the fourth quarter, sales rose 5 percent and orders were 5 percent higher, while operating profits were lower because of continuing pricing pressures in the components and energy products businesses and restructuring/unusual charges.
Component and energy product sales strengthened sequentially during the fourth quarter because of improved unit sales of end products and diversification of the customer base.
The Automotive and Industrial Electronics Group was awarded sensor business by a major U.S. automotive manufacturer for its model year 2000 vehicles.
Motorola Lighting began shipping new high-performance electronic ballasts to Asia. Space and Systems Technology Group
Group sales for the year rose 20 percent, orders were 49 percent higher than a year ago and operating profits were higher. Results are reported as part of the "Other Products" segment.

In the fourth quarter, sales increased 75 percent, orders were 18 percent lower and operating profits rose. No orders from Iridium LLC were booked during the fourth quarter, since orders in previous quarters had reached the present total financing available to Iridium LLC. As previously reported, Iridium LLC will require additional funding by late February 1997 to continue to make contractual payments to Motorola. Motorola is negotiating to increase its guarantee of Iridium LLC bank financing and these negotiations are expected to be completed by mid-February. There can be no assurances as to the outcome of these negotiations.
Development of the IRIDIUM(R), global communications system continued on schedule, as Motorola met all contractual milestones during the year. General Corporate

Manufacturing and other costs of sales increased to 68 percent of sales in the fourth quarter from 67 percent in the year-earlier period. For the full year, manufacturing and other costs of sales increased to 68 percent of sales versus 65 percent in 1995. This resulted from a more competitive pricing environment for semiconductors, modems, cellular telephones and pagers.

Selling, general and administrative expenses increased to 19 percent of sales in the fourth quarter versus 17 percent in the year-earlier period. This increase is attributable to the restructuring costs and other unusual charges recorded in the quarter. For the full year, selling, general and administrative expenses were 17 percent of sales, comparable to the percentage in 1995.
The tax rate for the year ended 1996 was 35 percent, compared with 36 percent in the prior year. Review and Outlook

Christopher Galvin, chief executive officer, said that the strategic decisions made in the fourth quarter are designed to set the stage for a renewal of growth in profitability later in 1997. "We have initiated a reinvigorated process of discontinuing those development programs that have not lived up to their promise, further reducing costs in existing businesses that are not achieving adequate profitability, and refocusing our investments where we possess, or are cultivating, leadership core competencies," he said.

"Motorola's Semiconductor Products Sector has begun to experience a sequential quarterly increase in orders and sales as the worldwide semiconductor industry enters a cyclical rebound, though improved year-over-year financial results may not be evident until later in 1997," he said. "We expect only gradual sequential improvement in semiconductor sales and earnings during the first stages of the industry recovery. The long-term outlook for our communications businesses is as promising as ever; however, many of the factors that affected certain of our businesses should continue to have an adverse impact in early 1997."

"Motorola is continuing to invest in programs that create platforms for future growth, such as IRIDIUM and flat-panel displays, without ignoring substantial investments in our core technology businesses," he said. As reported earlier, the start of the satellite deployment phase of the IRIDIUM program will result in much higher expenses being reported by Iridium LLC, as planned, of which approximately 25 percent are included in Motorola's financial results. These increased expenses are largely due to satellite depreciation before the system enters commercial service in late 1998. In addition, expenses in the flat-panel display business will increase significantly in 1997.

Galvin said the global economic outlook is healthy, "especially in emerging markets where Motorola is investing heavily, such as Latin America and Asia. We see balanced growth in the developed world as well. As the year progresses," he said, "we expect to reap more of the rewards of our investments in newer digital technologies derived from our core two-way radio, cellular, paging, satellite and wireline communications businesses. Motorola will continue to create products and technologies that will enable people to improve the way they live and work in ways they never expected." -0-
